references.text: The whole earth belongs to God, which supports the idea that the land cannot be sold permanently because it belongs to the Lord.
Heaven and earth belong to the Lord your God, confirming God's ownership over all the earth.
The earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, emphasizing God's sovereign ownership.
David describes himself as a stranger and guest with God, just as the Israelites are described in Leviticus.
The psalmist confesses to be a stranger on the earth, reflecting the status of being guests and strangers before God.
David acknowledges that the Israelites are strangers and guests before God's face, just like their fathers.
The heroes of faith confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth, reflecting the same idea of temporary residence.
Peter exhorts believers as strangers and foreigners, continuing the concept from Leviticus.
